definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.
For i∈J set e_i=Y_i(v)=y^i(v)/i!; the index i denotes its natural value.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

inputs.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

The family (e_i)_(i∈J) is a complex basis of V. One has y^(ell+1)v=0, and y^t v=0 for every natural t≥ell+1. Its generator actions are x e_0=0, x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤ell, y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<ell, y e_ell=0, and h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i for all i∈J.

For every complex vector space V, every index type I, endomorphism f, injective eigenvalue family μ:I→ℂ, and family a:I→V of nonzero f-eigenvectors with f(a_i)=μ_i a_i, the family a is complex-linearly independent.

hypotheses: V is a complex vector space and f is a complex-linear endomorphism.
For every i∈I, a_i≠0 and f(a_i)=μ_i a_i.

inputs.statement: For every field K, finite-dimensional K-vector space V, natural n, and independent family a:Fin n→V with dim_K V=n, the K-linear span of the range of a is all V.

hypotheses: K is a field and V is finite dimensional over K.

output.statement: The family (e_i)_(i∈J) is a complex basis of V. For every natural r and i∈J, X_r e_i=binom(ell−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and equals zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤ell and equals zero if i+r>ell. All binomial coefficients in these formulas are natural binomial coefficients mapped to ℂ. The subscript of an e vector is used only in the branch in which it lies in J.

argument.text: N007 states that e is a basis and h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. Each basis vector is nonzero: otherwise the coefficient family with 1 in that position would violate independence. Equality of two displayed complex weights cancels to 2i=2j and hence i=j because ℂ has characteristic zero. These facts supply exactly the eigenvector conditions and injective eigenvalue function.

produces.statement: For all i∈J, e_i≠0 and h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i, and i↦ell−2i is injective J→ℂ.

argument.text: Apply E001 using F001 and the operator h on the complex V. It yields independence of the family e.
H001 gives λ=(ell:ℤ) and dim_ℂ V=ell+1. Apply E002 to F002 to recover that e spans V. This verifies the basis clause of the asserted output from independence and spanning.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: For every i∈J and r≤i, iterate the x actions of N007 r times: x^r e_i=(∏_(a=1)^r(ell−i+a))e_(i−r). The r=0 product is 1; each next step multiplies by ell−i+r+1, which proves this by natural induction until the boundary. At r=i the resulting vector is a multiple of e_0, killed by x, so all powers with r>i vanish. Similarly, for i+r≤ell, iteration gives y^r e_i=(∏_(a=1)^r(i+a))e_(i+r); after reaching e_ell every further y gives zero. Dividing by r! as in D003–D004 gives the coefficients (ell−i+r)!/((ell−i)!r!)=binom(ell−i+r,r) and (i+r)!/(i!r!)=binom(i+r,r). These identities follow by cancellation in the factorial products and the defining factorial formula for the natural binomial coefficient; all factorials are nonzero in ℂ. In the vanishing branches the same scalar division gives zero. Indices of e appear only in their permitted branches. With F003 this is the asserted output for every natural r.
